title: Signature Quanta OS: The Conductor
description: Manon's Conductor concept: a quanta OS whose scheduler treats quantum and classical tasks as one orchestra — the classical optimizer and the QPU never wait on each other because the Conductor pipelines them like an assembly line. Its signature abstraction is the 'movement': a hybrid program section with declared quantum/classical phases the scheduler can interleave across jobs. Labeled Signature concept.

title: Signature Quanta OS: Qubit Tenancy
description: Manon's Qubit Tenancy concept: the OS leases qubits to programs the way landlords lease apartments — with contracts (qubit count, duration, fidelity SLA), eviction policies for hogs, and a public ledger of who holds what. A program that exceeds its fidelity budget gets migrated or paused, not silently corrupted. It applies operating-system fairness to a resource more precious than RAM. Signature concept.

title: Signature Quanta OS: The Noise Ledger
description: Manon's Noise Ledger concept: every qubit in the system carries a live ledger of its error history — gate errors, readout errors, drift — updated by every job and readable by every scheduler. The scheduler places sensitive operations on the quietest qubits automatically, and the ledger's history makes device comparisons honest. It turns calibration from a snapshot into a reputation. Signature concept.

title: Signature Quanta OS: Checkpoint Everything
description: Manon's Checkpoint Everything concept: the OS snapshots hybrid jobs at every classical-quantum boundary, so a failed QPU run resumes from the last checkpoint instead of restarting the thousand-iteration loop. Checkpoints are content-addressed and portable — move the job to a different backend and resume. It treats QPU time as too precious to ever waste twice. Signature concept.

title: Signature Quanta OS: The Honest Queue
description: Manon's Honest Queue concept: the job scheduler shows every user their true position, the jobs ahead, and why — no 'pending' black box. The concept argues that scarce shared hardware survives on legitimacy, and legitimacy requires transparency. Signature concept.

title: Signature Quanta OS: Pulse Sandbox
description: Manon's Pulse Sandbox concept: a safe playground inside the OS where users design custom pulses and test them on a simulator twin of the exact QPU before touching hardware — with a 'blast radius' limiter that rejects pulses that could damage or badly miscalibrate the device. Graduation from sandbox to hardware requires passing the twin's fidelity bar. It makes pulse-level research safe for non-experts. Signature concept.

title: Signature Quanta OS: The Fidelity Accountant
description: Manon's Fidelity Accountant concept: a compiler pass that attaches a predicted fidelity receipt to every compiled circuit — per-gate, per-qubit, per-readout contributions itemized — before anything runs. If the receipt predicts below the user's threshold, the compiler suggests concrete fixes: fewer SWAPs, different mapping, shallower ansatz. It makes fidelity a compile-time conversation. Signature concept.

title: Signature Quanta OS: Sleep Mode for Qubits
description: Manon's Sleep Mode concept: idle qubits are dynamically decoupled into protected states instead of sitting exposed to noise — the OS 'parks' qubits a job isn't using yet, cutting their effective error rate while they wait. Wake-up is a calibrated pulse sequence, and the scheduler accounts for wake latency. It treats qubit coherence as a budget the OS actively manages. Signature concept.

title: Signature Quanta OS: The Calibration Market
description: Manon's Calibration Market concept: QPU time is priced dynamically — fresh-calibration slots cost more, stale slots cost less, and users bid with priority points instead of money. The market clears every scheduling round, and the price history is public. It rations scarce premium hardware without a committee, using the oldest fair mechanism there is. Signature concept.

title: Signature Quanta OS: Crash-Only Qubits
description: Manon's Crash-Only concept, borrowed from classic systems design: quanta programs are written so any qubit can be re-initialized at any time without corrupting the computation — no graceful teardown, just crash and rebuild from checkpoints. The OS kills and restarts flaky qubits mid-job instead of nursing them. It trades elegance for the reality that qubits are the flakiest components ever put in a computer. Signature concept.

title: Signature Quanta OS: The Audit Trail
description: Manon's Audit Trail concept: every quantum job records an immutable trail — circuit hash, calibration snapshot, transpiler version, seed, results — so any result can be reproduced or challenged years later. 'A quantum result without a trail is a rumor.' The trail is the foundation of the field's credibility as results get harder to verify classically. Signature concept.

title: Signature Quanta OS: The Quiet Hours
description: Manon's Quiet Hours concept: the scheduler reserves nightly windows for long, delicate jobs — deep circuits, precision metrology — when the lab is thermally stable and nobody is opening fridge doors. title: Signature Quanta OS: The Onboarding Simulator
description: Manon's Onboarding Simulator concept: before a new user touches real QPU time, they qualify in a simulator twin that behaves like the device — same gate set, same noise model, same queue. The twin scores their circuits' efficiency and only graduates users whose jobs would not waste the hardware. It protects the scarce resource while training the next generation. This database's simulator is its prototype. Signature concept.
